bull.b: Rapid DTC growth and a larger share of sales give On greater control over customer relationships, presentation and product pricing. This channel mix can support brand consistency and margin durability while reducing reliance on third-party retail partners over the next several quarters.

The combination of substantial expected sales growth and high targeted margins indicates that On is scaling without sacrificing profitability. If achieved, these targets would support internally funded expansion, reinforce operating leverage and provide a durable earnings base through the forecast period.

Growth beyond core running footwear broadens On’s addressable demand and creates more opportunities to deepen customer engagement. Strong apparel and training performance, combined with advancing product technologies, can diversify revenue and sustain premium brand differentiation over time.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth and weaker sell-through in the Americas could constrain revenue cadence and increase channel volatility. Although management is reducing sell-in deliberately to protect full-price positioning, prolonged promotional conditions may make wholesale growth and inventory normalization less predictable.

A materially higher inventory balance increases the importance of disciplined sell-through and channel management. If demand or wholesale replenishment does not absorb the added units as planned, On could face greater working-capital needs or pressure to use promotions, potentially weakening cash conversion and margins.

bear.t: U.S. Tariff Cost And Timing Uncertainty
bear.b: Higher import tariffs create an external cost burden that can pressure margins or require pricing and sourcing responses. Because expected refunds are uncertain in timing and excluded from current guidance, the near-term earnings and cash impact may remain uneven while the company adjusts to the tariff environment.
